Studies have suggested that continuous antima- larial chemoprophylaxis with chloroquine during primary im- munisation with human diploid-cell rabies vaccine, given intra- dermally for pre-exposure prophylaxis, may be associated with a poor antibody response.1,2 WHO3 recommends that people cur- rently taking malaria prophylaxis or those unable to complete the 3-dose rabies pre-exposure regime before starting malaria prophy- laxis should receive pre-exposure rabies vaccination by the intra- muscular route instead. 1. Also available at: http://libdoc.who.int/ trs/WHO_TRS_931_eng.pdf (accessed 15/10/07) Uses and Administration Rabies vaccines are used for active immunisation against rabies. They are used as part of postexposure treatment to prevent rabies in patients who have been bitten by rabid animals or animals suspected of being rabid.
